item.content:encoded:
The definition of "cold-blooded" (well, the definition of "endothermic/poikilothermic", anyway, but I tried to avoid getting too technical) is "with an internal temperature that varies widely and is almost-entirely dependent on external sources for heat". When poikilotherms bask in the sun for heat, their temperature can be somewhat higher than that of their surroundings; otherwise, they're within a bare few degrees of the ambient temperature. SCP-799 can't differentiate temperature changes that small. (Put your hand on a piece of bare steel, then a piece of cloth; even if they're exactly the same temperature, they'll feel dramatically different. It'd be a heck of a poor survival trait for this thing to keep trying to eat polyester upholstery because it felt warmer than the wood frame of the chair.) So yeah, I think its limitation to homeothermic prey is pretty reasonable. *shrug*

I'm more interested in your critique of the expungements. Which, precisely, do you think need work?
